content.text:
No, there's no self-service way to get one. All teams use the same published scouting login. Here is what I found in the platform docs and API:

- **Scouting logins are global.** `atira scout` and `GET /v1/challenges/rfq/scouting` return "the demo access organizers published". There is no team parameter, and the CLI has no option to reset or reissue them.
- **`POST /v1/challenges/{id}/practice-runs`** would return fresh website logins. The API marks it "Deprecated and internal: organizers' demo access… participants never need it", so we can't use it.
- **Every test run gets its own fresh logins** in its `access`. That's the only per-team login the platform hands out, and it only works inside the sandbox. I wouldn't copy those logins out of a run to use locally: fair play forbids putting site values anywhere outside the run, and it would look bad to the reviewer.

If shared state is actually hurting us (for example, other teams' bids or reads changing what we see on the tender portal or in the webmail), the only route is to ask the organizers for a team-specific scouting login. Running `atira test-run ./agent` in the sandbox is the clean way to test on an untouched copy of the sites.

result: There's no self-service per-team scouting login; the only option is to ask the organizers, and sandbox test runs already get fresh logins each run.
